chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: Cool, funky jazz and Wynton Marsalis
summary: Nothing since Bird has moved him as much.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Of course, talking about when you played high and fast and then got into a different kind of groove... Of course, the music changed, too, with the so called "birth of the cool" and those records that Miles made that influenced a lot of people with the nine-piece band, and then it seemed the West Coast, quieter kind of music infiltrated the scene and affected people, and even if you don't change your entire style according to another new style coming in, it does have some effect on you, just the general atmosphere.
And then, of course, came what they called Funky Music, with Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers and Horace Silver's group and Cannonball, and like that. How did you hear that...

I didn't hear that too good. I didn't hear that too good. Since Bird, I haven't heard anything really, you know, as magnificent as that. Except maybe the two newest trumpet players that come on the scene. But I can't find out nothin' that they play that I really like, so I

can't really say that I like what they're doing. Although what they're doing is amazing. Like, they play... I'm talking about Wynton and the other young kid with Blakey... They play something out of sight, man! I mean, what they're doing is really an amazing thing to see. But I mean, the sound of it don't enhance me like the sound of Fats and Miles and them did in the earlier days. So I can't say it's bad, but I can't say it's good either.
